questions.question: Two individuals, A and B, have rented a field. A places 21 horses in the field for 6 months and 15 cows for 2 months. B adds 15 cows for 6 months and 40 sheep for 7.5 months. If 3 horses consume the same amount of food as 5 cows, and 6 cows eat as much as 10 sheep, what portion of the rent should A cover?
questions.questionHtml: Two individuals, A and B, have rented a field. A places 21 horses in the field for 6 months and 15 cows for 2 months. B adds 15 cows for 6 months and 40 sheep for 7.5 months. If 3 horses consume the same amount of food as 5 cows, and 6 cows eat as much as 10 sheep, what portion of the rent should A cover?
questions.solution:
⇒ 3 horses = 5 cows, 6 cows = 10 sheep

⇒ 1 horse = 5 ÷ 3 cows, 1 cow = 10 ÷ 6 sheep, 1 sheep = 3 ÷ 5 cow

⇒ A horses in cows = 21 × 5 ÷ 3 = 35 cows, A horses consumption = 35 × 6 = 210

⇒ A cows consumption = 15 × 2 = 30, Total A consumption = 210 + 30 = 240

⇒ B cows consumption = 15 × 6 = 90, B sheep in cows = 40 × 3 ÷ 5 = 24 cows

⇒ B sheep consumption = 24 × 7.5 = 180, Total B consumption = 90 + 180 = 270

⇒ Ratio A : B = 240 : 270 = 8 : 9, Portion of A = 8 ÷ (8 + 9) = 8 ÷ 17

questions.question: Two individuals, A and B rent a pasture. A uses 16 cows for a duration of 3 months and 20 sheep for 4 months and B uses 30 sheep for 6 months. If 4 cows are equivalent to 8 sheep, determine A's portion of the rent.
questions.questionHtml: Two individuals, A and B rent a pasture. A uses 16 cows for a duration of 3 months and 20 sheep for 4 months and B uses 30 sheep for 6 months. If 4 cows are equivalent to 8 sheep, determine A's portion of the rent.
questions.solution:
⇒ 4 cows = 8 sheep

⇒ 1 cow = 2 sheep

⇒ A cows in sheep = 16 × 2 = 32 sheep

⇒ A cows total consumption = 32 × 3 = 96

⇒ A sheep total consumption = 20 × 4 = 80

⇒ Total A consumption = 96 + 80 = 176

⇒ B sheep total consumption = 30 × 6 = 180

⇒ Ratio A : B = 176 : 180 = 44 : 45

⇒ Portion of A = 44 ÷ (44 + 45) = 44 ÷ 89

questions.question: Three groups of students have average ages 18, 20, and 22 respectively. If the number of students in the three groups is in the ratio 2:3:5, what is the overall average age?
questions.questionHtml: Three groups of students have average ages 18, 20, and 22 respectively. If the number of students in the three groups is in the ratio 2:3:5, what is the overall average age?
questions.solution:
Combined average = (18 × 2 + 20 × 3 + 22 × 5) ÷ (2 + 3 + 5)

⇒ Combined average = (36 + 60 + 110) ÷ 10

⇒ Combined average = 20.6

questions.question: The average of 11 numbers is 68. If the average of the first five is 63 and the average of the last five is 72, find the 6th number.
questions.questionHtml: The average of 11 numbers is 68. If the average of the first five is 63 and the average of the last five is 72, find the 6th number.
questions.solution:
Total of 11 numbers ⇒ 68 × 11 = 748

Total of first 5 numbers ⇒ 63 × 5 = 315

Total of last 5 numbers ⇒ 72 × 5 = 360

6th number ⇒ 748 − (315 + 360) = 73

questions.question: A fruit seller sells apples at a loss of 5% on the cost price but uses a weight that is 20% less than the actual weight. Find his total profit percentage.
questions.questionHtml: A fruit seller sells apples at a loss of 5% on the cost price but uses a weight that is 20% less than the actual weight. Find his total profit percentage.
questions.solution:
Let cost price of 1 kg = 100.

Selling price per kg at 5% loss = 100 × (1 − 5 ÷ 100) = 95.

Weight given = 1 − 20 ÷ 100 = 0.8 kg.

Effective selling price per actual kg = 95 ÷ 0.8 = 118.75.

Profit per kg = 118.75 − 100 = 18.75.

Profit % = (18.75 ÷ 100) × 100 = 18.75%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods at 60% above the cost price. He allows a discount of 25% on the marked price. If he also gives an additional cash discount of ₹150, and still makes a profit of 14% on the cost price, what is the cost price of the goods?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marks his goods at 60% above the cost price. He allows a discount of 25% on the marked price. If he also gives an additional cash discount of ₹150, and still makes a profit of 14% on the cost price, what is the cost price of the goods?
questions.solution:
<svg width="550" height="260" viewBox="0 0 550 260" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display:block;margin:1px;background:#ffffff;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid #cccccc;box-sizing:border-box;">
  <defs>
    <marker id="arr" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#2255cc"/></marker>
    <marker id="arrR" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#cc0000"/></marker>
    <marker id="arrG" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#007700"/></marker>
    <marker id="arrO" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#cc5500"/></marker>
  </defs>

  <!-- ZONE 1: PRICE LEVEL RULER -->
  <!-- CP Base -->
  <rect x="40" y="70" width="250" height="12" fill="#f0f0f0" stroke="#555555" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="40" y="60" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#555555">CP (100%)</text>
  
  <!-- Markup -->
  <rect x="290" y="70" width="150" height="12" fill="#ccffcc" stroke="#007700" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <path d="M290 45 Q365 30 440 45" fill="none" stroke="#007700" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#arrG)"/>
  <text x="325" y="25" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#007700">Markup +60%</text>
  <text x="410" y="60" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#007700">MP (160%)</text>

  <!-- Discount 1 (25% of 160 = 40%) -->
  <path d="M440 95 Q390 110 340 95" fill="none" stroke="#cc0000" stroke-width="1.5" marker-end="url(#arrR)"/>
  <text x="350" y="125" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#cc0000">−25% Disc.</text>
  <line x1="340" y1="70" x2="340" y2="95" stroke="#cc0000" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="4,2"/>
  <text x="315" y="145" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#2255cc">SP<tspan baseline-shift="sub" font-size="9">1</tspan> (120%)</text>

  <!-- Final Profit Level (114%) -->
  <line x1="325" y1="65" x2="325" y2="105" stroke="#007700" stroke-width="2"/>
  <text x="265" y="105" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#007700">SP<tspan baseline-shift="sub" font-size="9">final</tspan> (114%)</text>

  <!-- Cash Discount Gap -->
  <path d="M325 82 L340 82" stroke="#cc5500" stroke-width="1.5" marker-start="url(#arrO)" marker-end="url(#arrO)"/>
  <text x="315" y="170" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#cc5500">Gap = ₹150</text>
  <path d="M325 155 L325 145 Q332.5 135 340 145 L340 155" fill="none" stroke="#cc5500" stroke-width="1"/>

  <!-- ZONE 2: CALCULATION -->
  <text x="40" y="200" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">⇒ SP% after 25% discount = 160% × 0.75 = 120%</text>
  <text x="40" y="225" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">⇒ Cash Discount = 120% − 114% = 6% = ₹150</text>
  
  <text x="40" y="250" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#000000">∴ Answer = ₹2500</text>
</svg>

questions.question: How many approximate kgs of sugar costing ₹45 per kg must be mixed with 25 kg of sugar costing ₹32 per kg so that a 15% gain may be obtained by selling the mixture at ₹43.70 per kg?
questions.questionHtml: How many approximate kgs of sugar costing ₹45 per kg must be mixed with 25 kg of sugar costing ₹32 per kg so that a 15% gain may be obtained by selling the mixture at ₹43.70 per kg?

<svg width="480" height="300" viewBox="0 0 480 300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display:block;margin:1px;background:#ffffff;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid #cccccc;box-sizing:border-box;">

      <path d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z" fill="#cc5500"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>

  <!-- ZONE 1: Alligation Cross Mechanism -->
  <!-- Diagonal Lines -->
  <line x1="120" y1="50" x2="280" y2="150" stroke="#555555" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="4,2" />
  <line x1="280" y1="50" x2="120" y2="150" stroke="#555555" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="4,2" />

  <circle cx="120" cy="50" r="22" fill="#ddeeff" stroke="#2255cc" stroke-width="2" />
  <text x="120" y="55" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2255cc" font-weight="700">₹45</text>
  <text x="120" y="25" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#555555">Sugar 1</text>

  <circle cx="280" cy="50" r="22" fill="#f0f0f0" stroke="#555555" stroke-width="2" />
  <text x="280" y="55" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="#222222">₹32</text>
  <text x="280" y="25" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#555555">Sugar 2 (25 kg)</text>

  <!-- Mean Value (CP of Mixture) -->
  <circle cx="200" cy="100" r="25" fill="#ccffcc" stroke="#007700" stroke-width="2" />
  <text x="200" y="105" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="#007700" font-weight="700">₹38</text>
  <text x="200" y="72" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#007700">Mean CP</text>

  <!-- Gain logic annotation -->
  <path d="M230,100 Q260,100 260,85" fill="none" stroke="#007700" stroke-width="1" stroke-dasharray="2,2" marker-end="url(#arrG)"/>
  <text x="265" y="88" font-family="Arial" font-size="11" fill="#007700">(SP ₹43.70 @ 15% Profit)</text>

  <!-- Bottom Values (Difference / Parts) -->
  <rect x="100" y="150" width="40" height="25" rx="5" fill="#fff0cc" stroke="#cc5500" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <text x="120" y="167" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="#cc5500" font-weight="700">6</text>
  <text x="105" y="190" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#cc5500">Parts</text>

  <rect x="260" y="150" width="40" height="25" rx="5" fill="#fff0cc" stroke="#cc5500" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <text x="280" y="167" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="#cc5500" font-weight="700">7</text>
  <text x="295" y="190" font-family="Arial" font-size="12" text-anchor="middle" fill="#cc5500">Parts</text>

  <!-- Ratio connector -->
  <text x="200" y="167" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="#555555">Ratio = 6 : 7</text>

  <!-- ZONE 2: Solution steps -->
  <text x="30" y="225" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">⇒ CP of Mixture = 43.70 ÷ 1.15 = ₹38</text>
  <text x="30" y="248" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" fill="#222222">⇒ Required Qty = (25 kg ÷ 7) × 6 ≈ 21.42 kg</text>
  
  <text x="30" y="280" font-family="Arial" font-size="14" font-weight="700" fill="#000000">∴ Answer = 21 kg</text>
</svg>

questions.question: A triangular prism has base area of 25 cm². If height is increased by 20%, what is the new volume (original height was 10 cm)?
questions.questionHtml: A triangular prism has base area of 25 cm². If height is increased by 20%, what is the new volume (original height was 10 cm)?
questions.solution:
Original volume ⇒ 25 × 10 = 250 cm3

New height ⇒ 10 × (1 + 20 ÷ 100) = 12 cm

New volume ⇒ 25 × 12 = 300 cm3

questions.question: A circular disc's radius is decreased by 10%. What is the percentage decrease in its area?
questions.questionHtml: A circular disc's radius is decreased by 10%. What is the percentage decrease in its area?
questions.solution:
Let original radius = r

New radius = r × (1 − 10 ÷ 100) = 0.9r

Original area = πr2, New area = π × (0.9r)2 = 0.81πr2

Decrease in area = πr2 − 0.81πr2 = 0.19πr2

Percentage decrease = (0.19πr2 ÷ πr2) × 100 = 19%

questions.question: A vertical cylindrical container is filled with oil. A solid hemispherical stone of radius 7 cm is immersed completely, and the oil level rises by 3 cm. What is the radius of the cylinder?
questions.questionHtml: A vertical cylindrical container is filled with oil. A solid hemispherical stone of radius 7 cm is immersed completely, and the oil level rises by 3 cm. What is the radius of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
Volume of hemisphere = (2 ÷ 3)π × 73 = (686 ÷ 3)π

Volume rise in cylinder = πR2 × 3 ⇒ πR2 × 3 = (686 ÷ 3)π

3R2 = 686 ÷ 3 ⇒ R = √(686 ÷ 9) = √686 ÷ 3 ≈ 8.73 cm

questions.question: A sector of a circle has a central angle of 120° and a radius of 7 cm. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
questions.questionHtml: A sector of a circle has a central angle of 120° and a radius of 7 cm. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to the area of the second sector?
questions.solution:
⇒ Convert 120º into radians: 120º = 120 × π ÷ 180 = 2π ÷ 3 radians

⇒ Area of first sector = (1 ÷ 2) × 72 × (2π ÷ 3) = 49π ÷ 3

⇒ Area of second sector = (1 ÷ 2) × 72 × (2π ÷ 3) = 49π ÷ 3

⇒ Ratio = (49π ÷ 3) ÷ (49π ÷ 3) = 1 : 1
